messages:
sourabh: Heads-up — seeing a cluster of Xid 13 and 31 on a subset of A10 nodes in us-central-1 starting ~02:10 UTC. Pattern looks tied to short-lived decode bursts from tenant `deck-op` (small batches, frequent cold KV cache misses).

kai: can you paste the dmesg snippet + node list? are these all same BIOS/NIC driver?

sourabh: quick dump attached below. node set: a10-pool-usc-12..16 (5 nodes). NIC driver ixgbevf 5.2.1, kernel 6.1. We saw ECC correct counts creep up ~30m before Xid.

amanda: pasting dmesg sample (truncated):
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (13): 79, 0x0000000000000010
[ 12346.123456] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus: GPU 0000:af:00.0
[ 12346.123460] NVRM: Xid (31): 13, 0x00000000000000ff
[ 12346.123470] pcieport 0000:ae:00.0: AER: Corrected error; PCIe link degraded
[ 12346.123480] ixgbevf 0000:ae:00.1: NIC link down
```

jess: interesting — PCIe AER corrected + NIC link blips. not purely GPU thermal. any recent driver updates for runtime?

sourabh: runtime v2.3.1 deployed in that pool yesterday. We rolled back one node to v2.3.0 and ran the same small-batch replay; no Xid on that node during 20m test. The rest hit Xid within ~3 mins.

kai: can you repro with a targeted harness? run a small-batch decode load with KV cache cold-starts and tcpdump on vf interface. if NIC flaps then gpus might fall off bus and trigger Xid 13/31.

amanda: scheduling harness now on a single node (non-prod tag). command I used: `./perf_harness --model gpt-mini --batch-size 4 --qps 120 --kv-cold=true`

infra-bot: [alert] node a10-pool-usc-14 reported Xid 13 x3 in last 5m. Marking node as soft-drain candidate.

sourabh: hold on soft-drain — want to confirm whether it's runtime behavior or HW. if we drain immediately we lose the repro signal. propose: cordon + attach perf harness, run 10m, capture nvml, dmesg, tcpdump, and then soft-drain if Xid recurs.

jess: +1 to cordon-first. Also add `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=ecc.errors.corrected.total` poll every 30s to see ECC trend.

amanda: running with tcpdump and nvml collector. will upload logs to /mnt/tmp/xid-deckop-uscentral-233800

sourabh: early result: after ~2m of harness, we saw repeated PCIe corrected errors, then NIC vf link drop, then Xid 13. attaching pattern: ECC corrected up x10 -> PCIe AER -> Xid 13 -> short recovery -> repeat.

kai: does the affected node have any card-level microcode mismatch? check `nvidia-smi -q` and compare across pool. microcode looked identical when I checked yesterday but re-verify.

amanda: microcode strings: 96.02.XX across nodes, same. BIOS same too. but one node shows slightly higher therm delta on VRAM temps (+4C) under the same load.

jess: could be marginal signal integrity on that host's PCIe lane or a NIC firmware interaction under bursty small packets. two mitigations to test: 1) bump pcie_aspm to off for that node 2) upgrade NIC firmware to latest vendor quickpatch.

sourabh: quick tests: toggled `pcie_aspm` to off on one repro node, reran harness — no Xid after 15m. that's promising.

ops-bot: ops runbook note: if `pcie_aspm` off reduces repro, schedule a maintenance window to roll the change across the pool with canary. Document rollback path.

kai: let's not change firmware mid-week; plan: (a) patch pcie_aspm on canary nodes (b) run 24h soak with production-like traffic (c) if green, schedule NIC fw update next week in low-traffic window.

jess: also file a support ticket with Nvidia, include dmesg, nvml, and lspci+AER logs. they may trace to PCIe link retrain behavior on A10 under this runtime pattern.

amanda: filing ticket, attaching logs now. Ticket ID: NV-87621.

sourabh: next steps summary: cordon two suspect nodes, run harness + collectors, toggle pcie_aspm, verify ECC trend + AER events; if stable, soft-drain and apply config to rest with canary. I'll own rollout and SOP.

kai: thanks. also let's add a lightweight alert: if ECC corrected spikes > 50/min on a node, raise a warning in eng-sre channel before Xid cascade.

sourabh: will create alert: `gpu.ecc.corrected.rate` threshold 50/min for A10 pools.

infra-bot: action created: alert-rule/gpu-ecc-spike-A10 -> owners: eng-sre, eng-infra.

jess: nice detective work. once we confirm config fix, we should build a short blameless postmortem and add a test to the pre-deploy suite to replay small-batch KV-cold patterns.

sourabh: agreed. saving logs and timeline to the incident folder. will update thread after 24h canary. :thumbsup:

amanda: current status: canary node running with `pcie_aspm=off` for ~18m, no further Xid. continuing run.

ops-bot: reminder: if canary crosses 24h clean, create release PR for cluster config change with rollback steps.
